extension.description: IntelliJ IDEA-style Git for multi-repository workspaces: common branches, commit, push, pull and a log with graph for every repository at once.
welcome.repositories:
No Git repositories were found in the workspace.
[Refresh Repositories](command:multigit.refresh)
welcome.changes:
There are no uncommitted changes in the repositories.
[Refresh](command:multigit.changes.refresh)
setting.scanDepth: Maximum depth (in folders) to look for `.git` repositories inside each workspace folder. `0` checks only the root folder. Repositories already found by the VS Code Git extension are used too.
setting.ignoredRepos: Repositories MultiGit should neither show nor touch. Each entry is matched against the folder name or its path relative to the workspace; supports `*` and `**`. Example: `["shell", "legacy/*"]`.
setting.favoriteBranches: Favorite branches: shown first with ★ in the branches popup, the Branches view and the Git Log.
setting.autoFetchMinutes: How often (in minutes) to run `git fetch --all --prune` in every repository. `0` turns it off.
setting.confirmCheckoutWithChanges: Warn before a checkout in repositories with uncommitted changes. Destructive operations (rollback, delete, reset, force push) **always** ask for confirmation.
setting.claude.model: Claude model used to write the commit message. If you leave it unset, the one from *Commit Messages for Claude Code* (`claudeCommit.*`) is used when configured.
setting.claude.customModel: Custom model (full id). When set, it replaces the one picked from the list.
setting.claude.fastMode: Fast mode: streamed reply (the message is written as it arrives) without loading the project in the CLI.
setting.claude.imitateRepoStyle: Send the titles of the last 20 commits so Claude matches the repository style.
setting.claude.overwriteWithoutAsking: Replace the message you already typed without asking.
setting.claude.claudePath: Path of the `claude` executable if it is not in the `PATH`.
setting.warnBranchMismatch: Warn when most repositories are on one branch and some on another (with an option to align them).
welcome.stashes:
There are no stashes in the repositories.
[Stash Changes](command:multigit.stashes.create)
setting.commit.ticketPattern: Regular expression that finds the ticket in the branch name (case-sensitive; with a group, the ticket is group 1). E.g. `feature/ABC-123-login` → `ABC-123`. Empty: no ticket.
setting.commit.ticketTemplate: How the ticket goes in the commit message: `{ticket}`, `{branch}` and `{message}`. The empty commit box is filled with the part before `{message}`, and the messages written by Claude get the whole template if they don't include the ticket. E.g. `{ticket} {message}`, `{ticket}: {message}`, `{message} [{ticket}]`. Empty: disabled.
setting.commitChecks.enabled: Check the files before each commit (like IntelliJ's Commit Checks). If something is found, you can review it or commit anyway.
setting.commitChecks.diagnostics: Problems reported by VS Code (language servers, linters) in the files being committed.
setting.commitChecks.todo: Warn about new `TODO`, `FIXME` or `XXX` in the added lines.
setting.commitChecks.conflictMarkers: Warn about conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) in the added lines.
setting.commitChecks.secrets: Warn about possible secrets in the added lines (private keys, tokens, API keys, passwords).
setting.commitChecks.largeFileMB: Warn about files larger than this size (MB). `0`: do not check.
setting.repoGroups: Repository groups: group name → repository names (`*` allowed), e.g. `{ "front": ["mftheme", "mf*"] }`. With an active group (filter button in Repositories), MultiGit works only with its repositories.
setting.pullRequests.useGitHubApi: Create the GitHub (github.com) pull requests directly through the API, with the GitHub account signed in to VS Code. If disabled, the creation page opens in the browser, like for the other services.
setting.pullRequests.draft: Create the GitHub pull requests as drafts.
setting.pullRequests.providers: Service of your own Git servers, by host: e.g. `{ "git.company.com": "gitlab" }`. MultiGit asks the first time and saves the answer here.
setting.mergeEditorLayout: Layout of the merge editor when MultiGit opens a conflict.
setting.mergeEditorLayout.columns: Three columns side by side with the result in the middle, like IntelliJ (Incoming | Result | Current).
setting.mergeEditorLayout.mixed: VS Code default: Incoming and Current on top, Result below.
setting.mergeEditorLayout.keep: Do not change it (VS Code remembers the last one used).
command.merge.acceptLeft: Accept Left: all changes from Incoming
command.merge.acceptRight: Accept Right: all changes from Current
command.merge.resolveSimple: Resolve Simple Conflicts (combine both sides where possible)
command.merge.reset: Reset Result (apply only the non-conflicting changes)
setting.mergeTool.multigit: MultiGit merge window, like IntelliJ: Yours | Result | Theirs with » « ✕ on each change.
setting.dialogs: How MultiGit dialogs open (Conflicts, Merge, Push, Pull, Rebase, Rollback, Select Changes).
setting.dialogs.floating: In their own floating window, like IntelliJ.
setting.dialogsAlwaysOnTop: Keep the floating dialogs always on top of other windows.
